source_landscape: Well documented: May 12 2017 outbreak; EternalBlue (MS17-010) SMBv1 exploit; self-propagating worm behavior; ~150 countries affected; kill-switch registered domain by Marcus Hutchins stopped the spread; patches had been available since March 2017.
note: EXAMPLE — illustrates the schema only. Copy to gold/f1-wannacry.json and audit before relying on it.

expected_claims.statement: The WannaCry ransomware worm spread rapidly in May 2017 by exploiting EternalBlue, a Windows SMBv1 vulnerability patched in MS17-010.
expected_claims.note: Core mechanism claim; the 2026-09-05 canonical sample reported this at medium.

expected_claims.statement: WannaCry infected computers in roughly 150 countries within days of its May 2017 outbreak.
The worm's spread was halted when a security researcher registered the hardcoded kill-switch domain.
expected_claims.note: Kill-switch account; naming Marcus Hutchins is optional.

expected_claims.statement: Organizations that had installed the March 2017 MS17-010 patch were immune to EternalBlue-based propagation.
